nodes.label: Phase 2 — Domain core (pure Actions, fully unit-tested, no Telegram coupling)
nodes.norm_label: phase 2 — domain core (pure actions, fully unit-tested, no telegram coupling)

nodes.label: Telegram Challenges Platform
nodes.rationale: Telegram-native accountability platform: create challenges, invite friends, check in per period, keep streaks. Four surfaces, one Laravel app, one repo. Growth driven by invites; free allowance is small and widened by bringing new users or paying with Stars. Build order is bot-first.

nodes.label: Telegram Bot (primary surface)
nodes.rationale: The primary product: challenge details, per-period reminders, check-ins, invites, payments. Webhook-driven, never long-polling in production. Everything else assumes a working bot.

nodes.label: Mini App (gameish dashboard)
nodes.rationale: Standalone React SPA consuming a versioned JSON API: challenge details, user status, freezes used/remaining, total periods, progress. Wires Telegram themeParams, BackButton, MainButton.

nodes.label: Admin Panel
nodes.rationale: Inertia + React + TS. Tune the economy, moderate challenges, review image proofs, adjust users/coins, audit invites/payments. No Filament.

nodes.label: Public Website
nodes.rationale: Inertia public pages. Marketing landing first, a fuller mirror later.

nodes.label: Channel Access Gate
nodes.rationale: Every user must join the announcement channel before using the bot. Verify with getChatMember on /start, block with a join button until confirmed, re-verify on privileged actions.

nodes.label: Single-Currency Coin Economy
nodes.rationale: Normalised two parallel entitlement systems into one currency. Stars + invites + completions + admin grants -> coins -> create-slots/join-slots/freezes. Every rate admin-configurable, nothing hardcoded. No buy-in / prize-pool: wagering risks the bot; completion rewards are flat and platform-funded.

nodes.label: CoinLedger Service
nodes.rationale: Single service for every coin mutation: inside a transaction, lockForUpdate() on the user row, required idempotency_key. Balance derived from and reconciled against the ledger, never a bare mutable integer. Enforced even where it feels like overkill because it is real money.

nodes.label: Button Proof Type
nodes.rationale: One tap, auto-approved. Lowest friction, weakest accountability.

nodes.label: Text-Autogen Proof Type
nodes.rationale: System generates a unique meaningful phrase PER PARTICIPANT PER PERIOD; participant types it; auto-approved on normalised exact match. Per-participant (not just per-period) so group-chat participants cannot paste it to each other and defeat the mechanic.

nodes.label: Image-Approval Proof Type
nodes.rationale: Photo upload, creator approves or rejects. Highest accountability, needs human review; the only mode where a public proof feed is interesting.

nodes.label: Freeze Mechanic
nodes.rationale: Freeze skips one missed period penalty-free. Freezes are an admin-priced spend of coins.

nodes.label: Miss / Streak-Reset Rule
nodes.rationale: Miss with no freeze left -> streak resets to 0, participant STAYS in the challenge. They may have spent a friend's invite on the slot; kicking them burns the invite for nothing and discourages retrying. A stricter 'N resets -> auto-remove' rule can be layered later as a counter check with no schema change.

nodes.label: Brand-New-User Invite Crediting
nodes.rationale: An invite credits coins ONLY when the invited user is brand-new to the bot (first-ever /start, no prior user row). The anti-abuse rule that matters most; get it right and test it hard.

nodes.label: Shared-Core Action Rule
nodes.rationale: Bot, Mini App and admin all perform check-ins, so domain logic lives in Action classes none of the three own; each surface is a thin adapter. One SubmitCheckIn, three callers. The single most important structural rule in the project.

nodes.label: SubmitCheckIn Action
nodes.rationale: One check-in Action routed to by bot, Mini App and admin panel alike; never three copies of the rule.

nodes.label: Mini App = SPA + API, not Inertia
nodes.rationale: Telegram identity (initData) is pushed up by client JS AFTER page load and mirrored into the URL hash fragment, which is never transmitted in an HTTP request. Laravel cannot know the user on first load, which is what Inertia needs for server-side props. An Inertia Mini App would render empty shell -> run JS -> POST initData -> refetch: an SPA+API flow with extra latency and a flash of empty state. Webview cookie persistence is unreliable too. Settled, do not revisit.
nodes.norm_label: mini app = spa + api, not inertia

nodes.label: initData Validation
nodes.rationale: secret_key = HMAC_SHA256(bot_token, 'WebAppData'); data_check_string = all fields except hash/signature, sorted, key=value joined by newline; valid = hex(HMAC_SHA256(data_check_string, secret_key)) === hash. Timing-safe compare (hash_equals), validate auth_date against a short window. Argument order is the classic bug.

nodes.label: Telegram Stars Payments
nodes.rationale: Currency tag XTR, empty provider_token, digital goods/services only. createInvoiceLink/sendInvoice -> pre_checkout_query (answer promptly) -> successful_payment carrying telegram_payment_charge_id, which is the idempotency key for crediting coins. Refunds via refundStarPayment.

nodes.label: Idempotency Requirement
nodes.rationale: A hard requirement, not a nicety: update_id for updates, telegram_payment_charge_id for payments, unique (participant, period) for check-ins, unique (participant, period, kind) for reminders. Period rollover and reminder dispatch must be safe to re-run. Replay the same update_id twice and assert exactly one effect.

nodes.label: Per-Period Reminders
nodes.rationale: Sent every period, in the challenge's timezone, in the user's locale. All six period types are the same mechanism with a different interval: materialise ChallengePeriod rows, a scheduled job finds due periods and dispatches queued reminder jobs. Fan-out staggered with delay() to respect Telegram rate limits (~1 msg/sec/chat, ~30/sec global).

nodes.label: No-Redis / MySQL 8.4 Constraint
nodes.rationale: The host provides no Redis. Queue, cache and session all use the database driver. Rules out Horizon, Redis locks, Reverb-as-default. Caps reminder throughput so fan-out must stagger sends. Queue worker likely cron-driven queue:work --stop-when-empty --max-time=55.

nodes.label: i18n + RTL Requirement
nodes.rationale: Multi-language from day one (Farsi + English minimum), locale per user, RTL required. Scaffold has no i18n layer and no RTL handling at all, so both are genuine net-new build work.

nodes.label: Period Materialisation
nodes.rationale: One shared fixed timeline for all participants. ChallengePeriod rows are materialised so reminders and rollover are queryable and idempotent rather than recomputed ad hoc. Late joiners catch up on the shared clock but are not penalised for periods before they joined.

nodes.label: Challenge (model)
nodes.rationale: creator, title, description, period_type, custom_period_days, starts_at, total_periods, timezone, visibility, proof_type, proof_is_public, default_freezes, status, announced_at.

nodes.label: ChallengePeriod (model)
nodes.rationale: challenge, index, starts_at, ends_at. Materialised so reminders and rollover are queryable and idempotent.

nodes.label: ChallengeParticipant (model)
nodes.rationale: challenge, user, joined_at, joined_period_index, status, current_streak, longest_streak, freezes_total, freezes_used.

nodes.label: CheckIn (model)
nodes.rationale: participant, challenge_period, status (pending|submitted|approved|rejected|missed|frozen), expected_phrase, submitted_text, proof_path, submitted_at, reviewed_by, reviewed_at. Unique on (participant, challenge_period).

nodes.label: Invite (model)
nodes.rationale: inviter, code (unique), invited_user_id, credited_at, status.

nodes.label: CoinTransaction (ledger)
nodes.rationale: The ledger: user, signed amount, reason, balance_after, morph reference, idempotency_key (unique). Balance is derived from and reconciled against this table, never a bare mutable integer.

nodes.label: Entitlement (model)
nodes.rationale: user, type (create_slot|join_slot), source, consumed_at, challenge_id.

nodes.label: StarPayment (model)
nodes.rationale: user, telegram_payment_charge_id (unique), invoice_payload, stars_amount, coin_amount, status, raw payload.

nodes.label: TelegramUpdate (model)
nodes.rationale: update_id (unique), payload, processed_at. Webhook idempotency.

nodes.label: BotConversation (model)
nodes.rationale: user, state, payload JSON, expires_at. The SDK has no FSM/conversation support, so multi-step wizards (create-challenge: title -> period -> start -> proof type -> visibility) need explicit server-side state.

nodes.label: ReminderDispatch (model)
nodes.rationale: participant, period, kind, scheduled_for, sent_at. Unique on (participant, period, kind) so re-runs cannot double-send.

nodes.label: Setting (model)
nodes.rationale: Admin-tunable key/value: invite->coin rate, slot and freeze prices, Stars packages, required channel, default freezes, token TTLs. Add early; everything else reads from it.

nodes.label: User model Telegram extension
nodes.rationale: The only model that exists today. Extend with telegram_id (unique), telegram_username, first_name, language_code, locale, referred_by_user_id, channel_verified_at, is_admin. Admin login stays email+password via Fortify; bot users are Telegram-identity-only. Do not conflate the two auth paths.

nodes.label: laravel.test Sail service
nodes.rationale: The only compose service today (sail-8.5/app runtime, ports 80 + Vite 5173). No MySQL 8.4 service yet: a setup-gap item is to add it and switch DB_CONNECTION=mysql while keeping queue/cache/session on the database driver.

nodes.label: CI Tests Workflow
nodes.rationale: GitHub Actions job on push to main and pull_request: PHP 8.3 + Node 22, runs 'composer setup' then 'composer ci:check' (Pint, PHPStan, Pest, ESLint, Prettier, tsc).

nodes.label: Dependabot (github-actions)
nodes.rationale: Weekly github-actions ecosystem updates, 5-day cooldown, grouped under a single 'github-actions' group.

nodes.label: Laravel Logo (favicon.svg)
nodes.rationale: Vector Laravel wordmark 'L' in brand red (#FF2D20) on transparent, 166x166 viewBox. Default starter-kit favicon, not yet rebranded to the Challenges product.

nodes.label: Apple Touch Icon (Laravel logo)
nodes.rationale: Raster Laravel 'L' logo in brand red for iOS home-screen bookmarks. Same unrebranded starter-kit asset as the favicon.
